'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant crisis]]
****The [[Russian occupation of Zaporizhzhia Oblast|Russian-controlled]] [[Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant]] in [[Enerhodar]] is [[Shell (projectile)|shelled]], with damage occurring to some buildings, systems, and equipment, according to the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-says-ukraine-shells-zaporizhzhia-nuclear-power-plant-tass-2022-11-20/ (Reuters)]
*[[Kurdish–Turkish conflict]], [[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Operation Claw-Sword]]
***The [[Turkish Air Force]] launches a series of [[airstrike]]s against the [[Kurds in Syria|Kurdish]]-led [[Syrian Democratic Forces]] (SDF) and [[Syrian Army]] positions in [[Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria|Northern]] [[Syria]], and the [[Kurdistan Workers' Party]] (PKK) in [[Iraqi Kurdistan]] following the [[2022 Istanbul bombing|Istanbul bombing]], which [[Ankara]] blames on [[Kurdish nationalism|Kurdish separatists]]. The [[Syrian Observatory for Human Rights]] reports that at least 35 people were killed, including 18 SDF fighters and 16 Syrian troops. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/11/20/turkey-launches-air-raids-in-syria-iraq-over-istanbul-blast (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.syriahr.com/%d8%a8%d8%b6%d8%b1%d8%a8%d8%a7%d8%aa-%d8%ac%d9%88%d9%8a%d8%a9-%d8%aa%d8%b1%d9%83%d9%8a%d8%a9-%d8%a7%d8%b1%d8%aa%d9%81%d8%a7%d8%b9-%d8%b9%d8%af%d8%af-%d9%82%d8%aa%d9%80-%d9%80%d9%84%d9%89-%d9%82/571734/ (SOHR)]
*[[Insurgency in Cabo Delgado]]
**A [[humanitarian aid]] worker for the French [[Non-governmental organization|NGO]] [[Solidarités International]] and a few other civilians are killed in an ambush in the [[Cabo Delgado Province]] of [[Mozambique]]. [https://www.news360.es/ireland/2022/11/23/aid-worker-killed-in-ambush-in-mozambique-5/ (News360)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Egypt–Turkey relations]]
**[[President of Egypt|Egyptian president]] [[Abdel Fattah el-Sisi]] and [[President of Turkey|Turkish president]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] meet for the first time following their opposing involvements in the [[2013 Egyptian coup d'état]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/middle-east/erdogan-sisi-meet-in-qatar-for-the-first-time-amid-strained-ties (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Colorado Springs nightclub shooting]]
**Five people are killed and 25 others injured in a [[mass shooting]] at a [[gay bar]] in [[Colorado Springs]], [[Colorado]], [[United States]], during a [[drag show]] and a commemoration of the [[Transgender Day of Remembrance]]. A suspect is taken into custody shortly afterward. [https://www.cnn.com/2022/11/20/us/colorado-springs-shooting-gay-nightclub (CNN)]
*Two people are killed and two others are seriously injured after a [[Vehicle-ramming attack|car hit a group of people]] in [[Oldbury, West Midlands]], [[United Kingdom]]. A suspect has been arrested by [[West Midlands Police]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-birmingham-63702591 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2022 Malaysian general election]]
**The results from yesterday's election indicate that [[Malaysia]] will experience a [[hung parliament]] in the [[Dewan Rakyat]] for the first time in its history. [https://edition.cnn.com/2022/11/19/asia/malaysia-election-race-parliament-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)]
**[[Leader of the Opposition (Malaysia)|Opposition leader]] [[Anwar Ibrahim]], whose [[Pakatan Harapan]] coalition won the most seats, and former [[Prime Minister of Malaysia|prime minister]] [[Muhyiddin Yassin]] of [[Perikatan Nasional]] both claim to have the necessary support to establish a new [[Government of Malaysia|government]], but neither have announced the [[List of political parties in Malaysia|parties]] involved. [https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/nation/2022/11/20/muhyiddin-hadi-meet-sarawak-premier-abang-johari/ (Free Malaysia Today)]
*[[2022 Kazakh presidential election]]
**[[Kazakhs]] head to the polls to elect their [[President of Kazakhstan|president]] in a [[snap election]]. [[Exit poll]]s suggest that [[President of Kazakhstan|President]] [[Kassym-Jomart Tokayev]] will be re-elected to a seven-year term. [https://www.trtworld.com/asia/polls-open-for-snap-kazakhstan-presidential-election-62714 (AFP via TRT World)] [https://www.dw.com/en/kazakhstan-election-tokayev-set-for-landslide-exit-polls/a-63818194 (DW)]
*[[2022 Equatorial Guinean general election]]
**[[Equatorial Guinea]]ns head to [[polling place|the polls]] to elect their [[President of Equatorial Guinea|president]] and members of [[Parliament of Equatorial Guinea|parliament]]. [https://www.citizen.co.za/news/news-world/news-africa/equatorial-guinea-ruler-seeks-re-election/ (AFP via ''The Citizen'')]
*[[2022 Nepalese general election]]
**[[Nepalis]] head to the polls to elect the 275 members of the [[House of Representatives (Nepal)|House of Representatives]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2022/11/20/Voting-begins-in-Nepal-amid-concerns-over-economic-political-stability (Al Arabiya)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2022 FIFA World Cup]]
**The 22nd edition of the [[FIFA World Cup]] opens in [[Qatar]], with [[Ecuador national football team|Ecuador]] defeating [[Qatar national football team|the hosts]] 2–0 in the [[2022 FIFA World Cup Group A#Qatar vs Ecuador|opening match]] at the [[Al Bayt Stadium]] in [[Al Khor]]. Qatar becomes the first host nation to lose their opening match in World Cup history. [https://apnews.com/article/world-cup-sports-soccer-qatar-middle-east-11a629d964a0c052fd01faa50722a70e (AP)]
*[[109th Grey Cup]], [[2022 CFL season]]
**The [[Toronto Argonauts]] defeat the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] 24–23 to secure their 18th [[Canadian Football League]] championship. [https://www.cbc.ca/sports/football/cfl/blue-bombers-argonauts-2022-cfl-grey-cup-recap-1.6658338 (CBC)]
*[[2022 ATP Finals]]
**[[Novak Djokovic]] of [[Serbia]] defeats [[Casper Ruud]] of [[Norway]] in two [[Tennis scoring system|sets]], 7–5, 6–3, to win his sixth [[ATP Finals]] title, equaling [[Roger Federer]]'s record. Djokovic becomes the oldest [[Types of tennis match#Standard types of match|singles]] champion at 35 years old. He also claims the biggest payday in tennis history, a record $4,740,300 in prize money. [https://mb.com.ph/2022/11/21/djokovic-sweeps-past-ruud-to-win-sixth-atp-finals-crown/ (AFP via ''Manila Bulletin'')]
